name: COVID-19 market crash
description: Growth collapse and credit stress overwhelm a government-bond rally; USD demand weakens EUR.
basis: All five shocks are illustrative assumptions, not observed returns. Net window assumes lower yields despite interim Treasury selling.

name: US inflation shock
description: Higher yields, equity losses and a stronger USD after the CPI surprise; HY widens while IG is unchanged.
basis: Reuse cached September research: 10Y +5.37bp, US IG/HY OAS 0/+18bp, S&P −4.32%, EUR/USD −1.46%. Illustrative parallel-rate, global-equity and European-credit mappings; asynchronous quotes, not authenticated portfolio returns.

name: Regional banking crisis
description: Safety demand lowers yields; banking contagion widens credit and weighs on equities. Lower US rate expectations support EUR.
basis: All five shocks are illustrative assumptions for Friday March 10 to Monday March 13, not observed returns. Parallel rates miss the larger front-end repricing; no bank-specific/default loss is modeled.

name: Yen carry-trade unwind
description: Deleveraging depresses equities and widens credit; a modest haven rally lowers yields. EUR strengthens slightly against USD.
basis: All five shocks are illustrative assumptions between Friday August 2 and Monday August 5 trading sessions; August 3–4 is the weekend. EUR/USD does not capture JPY directly; no yen exposure, leverage or margin loss is modeled.
